category: meta indexer over public trackers (JSON API, no key)

free_tier.stated: No key and no account: GET https://api.knaben.org/v2/search?q=... returned hits with hash, magnetUrl, tracker, seeders and bytes. The docs publish no quota.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: results are metadata and magnets

retention.stated: the database keeps documents after they go dead; the docs say 1.7 million documents were seen in the last week and the 'dead' flag is opt-in

egress.terms: no byte allowance: the API returns JSON records and magnets

interface_detail: GET /v2/search and GET /v2/browse with query parameters (q, sf, c, t, o, d, s, f, xxx, unsafe, dead, seen); size maximum 300. v1 still exists as POST /v1 with a JSON body. There is also an RSS page at knaben.org/rss/.
tooling: One GET. Sonarr/Radarr-style clients reach it through Torznab proxies; TorrentClaw lists Knaben as one of its sources, so the API is already the feed behind another index.
chaining: Query by title, take the magnetUrl or hash, hand the hash to a debrid service's cache check, and only fetch the ones that come back cached.

limits.value: the operator published a temporary rate of 1 request per 2 seconds on 2026-08-12, after a record of 25 million requests in a single day; the v2 docs state 'Size of the response, maximum is 300'. The status page of 2026-09-29 reads 'Now set up new network routing. Let's see how this goes...'

limits_note: v2 moved from POST to GET so the edge can cache the responses, which is a bandwidth measure. The operator published a temporary 1 request per 2 seconds limit on 2026-08-12 and later reported bandwidth maxed out; the 300-result ceiling remains in the v2 docs.
binding_note: The operator published a temporary 1 request per 2 seconds limit on 2026-08-12 and names bandwidth as the failure mode; no byte quota exists on this side.

identity_cost.detail: No key, no account, no captcha on the GET requests made today.

reliability_note: Bandwidth pressure is stated by the operator, and the API answers are edge-cached (Cache-Control public with s-maxage 300), so a stale page can show a torrent that has since gone dead.
confidence_note: Both doc pages and a live v2 response were read on 2026-10-23. A sustained poll with recorded statuses would raise the rate row to measured.

notes: The best machine-readable torrent feed in the sector that needs nothing: no key, documented parameters, 300 results per call, and a magnet in every hit that carries a hash. Its weakness is exactly the thing the sector asks about: the vendor publishes no rate, only a threat.
